subject: ventures/brevo-contacts-csv-check
professional: an email-marketing operations specialist (agency or in-house) who imports client contact lists into Brevo every week; first checks: which columns Brevo accepts as a contact identifier, SMS numbers in international form, duplicates (email and SMS), delimiter/encoding from European Excel, date attribute format, and that nothing touches consent

evidence.correctness: help.brevo.com and developers.brevo.com return proxy 403 / ENOTFOUND in this session, so Brevo's rules were taken from web-search snippets of Brevo's own help articles 208729849 ('Create a file to import your contacts': identifiers EMAIL, SMS, WHATSAPP, LANDLINE_NUMBER or EXT_ID, at least one required; 250MB file limit; one sheet) and 208723969 / 115000719584 (numbers without '+' and country code get the country chosen at import; a leading single quote is allowed), plus RFC 4180, RFC 5321 dot-atom and ITU E.164. 16 adversarial CSVs run through calc.mjs (scratchpad brevo/adv.mjs). Pass: UTF-8 BOM + CRLF (2 rows, no findings), RFC 4180 quoted comma (no extra-cells), semicolon delimiter (warning + repaired to commas), case-only duplicate email (dup-email on line 3), SMS without '+' (0612345678 and 33612345678 flagged), blank rows (skipped and noted), apostrophe-prefixed SMS (accepted). Fail: a consistent day-first column (03/04/2026, 15/04/2026) raises 'mixes date formats' with the text '1 day/month/year style and 1 day/month/year style'; an EXT_ID-only file gets error missing-column and a WHATSAPP-only row gets error no-identity 'this row will be skipped', contradicting Brevo's identifier list; a..b@, .a@, a@example..com and a@-example.com all pass as valid emails (RFC 5321 dot-atom forbids them); two contacts with the same SMS are not flagged; 0086 + 15-digit E.164 number (17 digits with prefix) gets a false 'more than 15 digits' warning.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features (README, page, llms.txt) checked end to end in Chromium: invalid and duplicate emails (works), rows with neither email nor SMS (works, but wrong for WhatsApp/EXT_ID/landline identifiers), SMS without country code (works), Excel scientific notation (works), >15 digits (works, false positive with 00 prefix), unquoted commas (works), mixed date formats (partial: false positive on consistent day-first columns, visible in the tool's own 'example with errors'), near-miss column names (works for the NEAR synonym table; a typo like FIRSTNAM is not suggested although closestColumn exists and is tested), safe fixes (works: delimiter, header spelling, trims; consent untouched), findings CSV download (works), opt-out usage counting (works). No stubs or TODOs.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' in the subject: 30 tests, 30 pass, 0.16 s. Mutations via quality_mutate.py: dup-email lower-casing removed -> caught; 00/+ prefix check loosened to 0 -> caught; sms-length '> 15' -> '>= 15' -> SURVIVED (no 15-digit boundary test); date ambiguity 'm[1] <= 12' -> '< 12' -> SURVIVED (no day=12 boundary test). The date-mixed test asserts only that mixing ISO and slash dates warns, never that a consistent column does not, which is how the false positive shipped. The fuzz test checks repair idempotence only.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (272 lines), index.html, usage.mjs, all tests. Pure, small, no dependencies, findings carry line numbers and the parser tracks physical lines through quoted newlines. Defects: closestColumn (calc.mjs:83) is exported and tested but never called by validate, so the Levenshtein suggestion is dead code on the user path; NEAR entries firstname/lastname are unreachable because canon() maps them to ROLE_OF first; detectDelim (calc.mjs:93) counts separators on the raw first line, so a quoted header containing a comma in a semicolon file ('"Name, full";EMAIL') picks comma and reports 'No EMAIL or SMS column'; dateShape returns two kinds ('ambiguous', 'slash') for one format.
evidence.claims: Backed: 'never leaves the browser' (Playwright saw zero non-local requests; page.test asserts no fetch/XHR), disclaimer and no-warranty footer (index.html:127), independence/trademark note (index.html:128), usage events named on the page match record() calls and localStorage after the walk held {file_checked:1, fixes_applied:1}, 'read from memory' honestly stated. Not backed: 'Every row needs an EMAIL or an SMS number' (index.html:96) and the error 'this row will be skipped' contradict Brevo's documented identifiers (also WHATSAPP, LANDLINE_NUMBER, EXT_ID); 'mixed date formats' fires on unmixed columns; llms.txt:5 says 'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in', boilerplate that does not describe a CSV checker. llms.txt URLs are github.io/github.com in source but served-copy.mjs reports no placeholder or retired origin in the served copy, so not filed.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job in headless Chromium against a local static server: chose a BOM + CRLF semicolon file with a quoted '; ' name, a spaced email, a national SMS, an E-notation SMS, a case-only duplicate email, day-first dates and a trailing blank row. Report: 1 error, 4 warnings, each with a line; Safe fixes listed the delimiter conversion and the trim; Download cleaned CSV produced comma-delimited text with the email trimmed and nothing else changed. A specialist gets real value on a typical email+SMS list, but would hit in the first hour: false 'mixed date' warnings on every European day-first file, false errors on WhatsApp/EXT_ID imports, no duplicate-SMS check (an SMS number can belong to only one Brevo contact), and invalid dot-atom emails passed. No horizontal scroll at 375 px, no page errors.
evidence.domain: Compared with Brevo's import help as quoted in search snippets (identifier list, '+' and country code or the import-time default country, single-quote prefix, 250MB/one sheet), RFC 5321 local-part/domain syntax and E.164. Departs: identifier set limited to EMAIL/SMS; no SMS uniqueness check; 00-prefixed numbers accepted silently although Brevo's help says numbers without '+' get the default country code applied; E.164 length counted including the 00 prefix; 'about 30' attribute limit at calc.mjs:15 is uncited. The consent handling, Excel-damage detection and country-code refusal to guess are what a practitioner would want.

defects.what: A column of consistently day-first dates (03/04/2026 and 15/04/2026) is warned as 'mixes date formats' with the self-contradictory text '1 day/month/year style and 1 day/month/year style': dateShape returns 'ambiguous' and 'slash' as different kinds for the same format. Fires on the tool's own 'example with errors' and on most European files.

Only EMAIL and SMS are treated as identifiers; Brevo also creates contacts from WHATSAPP, LANDLINE_NUMBER or EXT_ID. An EXT_ID-keyed file gets error 'No EMAIL or SMS column' and a WhatsApp-only row gets error 'this row will be skipped', both wrong; the page repeats the rule.
Duplicate SMS numbers across different contacts are not flagged, although SMS is a unique contact identifier in Brevo.
EMAIL regex accepts RFC 5321-invalid addresses: consecutive dots (a..b@, a@example..com), leading dot in local part, hyphen-leading domain label.
sms-length counts the 00 international prefix as part of the E.164 number, so a valid 15-digit number written 00... gets a false 'more than 15 digits' warning.
Boundary mutants survive: no test pins a 15-digit SMS or a day=12 date, and no test asserts a consistent date column is not 'mixed'.

closestColumn (Levenshtein typo suggestion) is exported and unit-tested but never called by validate, so a header typo like FIRSTNAM gets no suggestion; NEAR firstname/lastname entries are unreachable.
detectDelim counts separators on the raw first line, ignoring quotes: a semicolon file whose header has a quoted comma is parsed as comma-delimited and reported as 'No EMAIL or SMS column'.
llms.txt says 'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in', calculator boilerplate that does not describe a CSV checker.
Attribute-count warning asserts Brevo allows 'about 30' contact attributes with no citation.

verdict: A compact, honest, private checker that does the core Brevo import checks (BOM/CRLF/quoted commas, semicolon repair, case-only duplicate emails, SMS without '+', Excel E-notation) correctly and walks end to end in the browser with local-only usage counts and a proper disclaimer. It does not meet the bar: 5 of 9 correctness/domain checks against Brevo's documented rules, RFC 5321 and E.164 failed. The worst is a false 'mixes date formats' warning on any consistent day-first date column (shown in its own error example), followed by treating only EMAIL/SMS as identifiers when Brevo also accepts WHATSAPP, LANDLINE_NUMBER and EXT_ID, and no duplicate-SMS check. Two of four seeded boundary mutants survived. Brevo's help pages were unreachable from this session (proxy 403); Brevo rules were taken from search snippets of its help articles.
